reviews.review: Endless Giant Insect Killing with a variety of weapons, what more can you ask for?

The most recent in the Earth Defense Force series, it continues the series tradition of being a simple, yet thoroughly enjoyable third-person shooter, but this one tries to introduce some sorely-needed quality of life changes for EDF. Item grinding, while present, is nowhere near as tedious as 4.1 and there's more polish here and there, with the game having a tutorial, slightly more emphasis on story happenings, and more options and nuance for characters.

There's far more missions than 4.1, and they tend to hit similar story beats and setpieces as the previous game, but this tends to lead to a lot of fatigue as the game feels not as well-paced as a result. Beyond that, this game does not have any particular weakness not already present in preceding games in the series, but it still bears repeating - these are very simple games, for better or worse. Shoot enemies until the map is cleared, rinse, repeat. It's not a AAA experience, and that's not necessarily a bad thing.

When it comes to local multiplayer options, this game actually fares a little worse than 4.1, surprisingly. A local co-op player will not start with the same armor values as the main player, which is a little less comfy than 4.1's setup. There is also no local battle/versus mode like 4.1 - not a selling point nor anything particularly deep, but mildly disappointing if you like to take the Air Raider's Speed Star with a friend on an otherwise empty map and just goof around.

And I will say, unlike 4.1, the DLC for this game is far more worthwhile, with some very high-end weapons available.

If you love EDF, this does not disappoint. If you love third-person shooters but want something really straightforward, give this series a try.

It's EDF, that alone is a seal of warranty. The gameplay has improved from the previous entries. There are new stages and monsters to fight. The npc dialogues are hilarious as usual. The only thing that doesn't feel quite as satisfying is the anthem. EDF 4 had a much better one. Still, very recommended if you like to fight hordes of aliens and giant bugs with style.
